result.topic_en: Notes on Abelian functions (August–September 1855): an algebraic curve F(x^{n+1}, y^{n+1}) = 0 and later F(x^n, y^m) = 0, counting double points and constants, writing the Abelian differentials φ dx / F'(y) = -φ dy / F'(x), and computing the number of branch points w and the genus p = 2((n-1)(m-1) - α).

methods.what: Differentiating the curve equation F = 0 to relate dx and dy, giving the form of the Abelian differential
Abelian integral of the first kind on a curve F(x^n, y^m) = 0, with numerator of degree n-2 in x and m-2 in y
Relation between the number of branch points w of y as a function of x and the invariant p
Branch-point count reduced by double points
Genus-type formula for a curve of bidegree (n, m) with α double points
Constant count for the curve of degree n+1, with α = n(n-1) relations
Weighted sum over singular points (multiplicities) that adjusts the branch-point count
